Guidance & outlook: I don't expect currencies to be less volatile, nor do I expect the business environment not to kind of become more and more complex as we go.
When it comes to FY27 and we've touched base upon FY27 a few times in the last couple of months.
Yeah, we will do that in a manner in which we kind of hold the guidance and we don't kind of re deliver this guidance.
Growth & demand: Double-digit volume growth, and the thinking was once we get to double- digit volume growth, automatically the profits will follow.

I mean, penetration moving up from close to 65% to 80%, and volumes growing at a CAGR of 15% in the last few years is actually really good news because it just means that the need from the consumer for this category is there.
We're unlikely to kind of take on something which is going to be a 10 %, 15% growth.
Margins & costs: Cost saving and simplification, I think we've done an extremely good job simplifying our operations, specially the international operations, and kind of ensuring that we release cost and release again bandwidth of the resources.
The USG has been 7% and 6%, and EBITDA has been 6%.

All of this put together, just from an investment of costs and resources, it is likely to be close to INR200 crores per annum in the fullness of time, which is likely to be around 12 months, we should be able to complete this journey.
Capex & expansion: If it is a multiplier where we can kind of acquire an asset and make it 3x, 4x in a defined period of time, we would be more than happy to kind of pick it up if it is a strategic category for us and if it kind of gives us an EPS break-even soon.
On capex, we've finished the big capex cycles, and most of them will get complete in this year.
The INR 150 crores which I talked about was a capex investment in in the R&D facility.
Balance sheet & cash: We moved into a rhythm of dividend payout every quarter, and we've got the health of the business, both from a P&L perspective and the balance sheet, much stronger.
Volumes results in revenue, revenue gives us not only leverage, but then profits.
In terms of capital allocation, we've spoken about the dividend policy, we're committed to it.
Risks & challenges: Having said that, macros have been volatile, commodity prices have been fairly volatile and have been inflated in nature.
Currencies have been volatile significantly, and we do have a sizable international business.
At the same time, the business context and competition has been evolving.

Guidance & outlook: Since we anticipate a lot of questions, we request all of you to please limit to two questions per turn, and then to reapply for the turn.

It moves the conversation from "Did we meet the plan?" to a harder question, if we put our hands on our hearts, "Does this really meet our high expectations?" I talked about the outstanding success of incense sticks, but how liquid vaporizers has not met our high ambitions post -RNF.
This has resulted in EBITDA margins growing significantly, from 9% to 10% in FY24 to 15% in FY26.
Growth & demand: The guidance remains unchanged: high-single -digit volume growth, double-digit revenue growth, double -digit profit growth.
First is broad -based volume growth globally, getting more households to use our categories more often.
Second, top-line growth that converts into profit growth over a reasonable period of time.
Margins & costs: Africa's rapidly grown its margin-accretive FMCG portfolio, headlined by the highly successful launch of our air care category, while strengthening its traditional hair fashion business.
We fixed the fundamentals, double media investments, grew the business in strong double digits, and the margin improvement came with that.

I think on LV, LV Abneesh, we've done okay, but my expectations post this, like I mentioned incense stick has been a huge success, really good for GCPL, I think it's an 85 sort of percent of our normative margin.
Capex & expansion: This Muuchstac acquisition has been very successful for us, and we're already putting other GCPL brands using that model there.
When it comes to inorganic acquisitions, and I think Pet in a way is similar, because it's like completely a new category with a lot to be done in terms of building the GTM, making these investments.
Risks & challenges: I think one of the things that I've seen in the Africa business, which you all have seen the numbers of many years, it's a challenging, very challenging operating environment.

I think I think one is wherever there has been a challenge, I think what we picked up is that I think it's important to kind of lay down and we have been kind of practicing this whole framework of solved-unsolved.
I think A asif is feeling the pressure already from me, that this is very much what you've developed, delivered in Africa, you better pull it across the whole company and do it quickly.

guidance.t: The guidance remains unchanged: high-single -digit volume growth, double-digit revenue growth, double -digit profit growth.

Guidance & outlook: There has also been a structural improvement in EBITDA from high single digit to a consistent mid -teens level, and we are confident of holding this going forward.
With revenue growth tracking ahead of our original expectations and input costs beginning to ease, we enter the remainder of FY27 with increased confidence.
We remain confident in the resilience of our portfolio, the strength of our brands and our ability to deliver sustained profitable growth going forward.
Growth & demand: At a consolidated level, revenues grew 19% year -on-year with underlying volume growth of 9%.
This quarter, consolidated underlying volume growth reached 9%, supported by increasingly broad-based momentum across geographies and categories.

I would say in the longer term, you may or may not get 17% volume growth may not be what we may sustainably get even with FMCG growth because as I told you that there are volatile continent, but it will still, I suspect, be much better than what we've had in the past.
Margins & costs: Net profit grew 11%, reflecting healthy underlying earnings quality, even as margins absorb some near-term commodity pressure.
In Q1, we experienced significant input cost inflation and instability with LPG prices going up 3x and similar increases in other costs.
If I heard right, we saw a blended cost inflation of 6%, and we took a blended price hike of 5%.
Capex & expansion: This was on the back of a strong broad-based performance in India, Indonesia coming back to stable growth and an exceptional performance in Africa driven by FMCG expansion.
Obviously, you've acquired Muuchstac and obviously your M&A team is very active in terms of looking at opportunities.
I think since we took over the acquisition itself, I think we have grown by about 70% or 80% from the run rate.
Risks & challenges: The operating environment remained challenging through much of the quarter.
But look, our target is to be in this 22% to 26% kind of margin for India even in a weak quarter.
I know you just mentioned about 22% to 26%, but is this just rehashing because of the volatility.

guidance.t: But look, our target is to be in this 22% to 26% kind of margin for India even in a weak quarter.
